drills.q: Write a top-5-salaries query two ways and explain why the naive version fails.
drills.a: Naive: SELECT name, salary FROM employees WHERE ROWNUM <= 5 ORDER BY salary DESC — ROWNUM assigned pre-sort = five arbitrary rows, sorted. Correct legacy: SELECT * FROM (SELECT name, salary FROM employees ORDER BY salary DESC) WHERE ROWNUM <= 5. Modern: ORDER BY salary DESC FETCH FIRST 5 ROWS ONLY.

drills.q: Why does WHERE ROWNUM = 2 return zero rows?
drills.a: ROWNUM is assigned incrementally as rows satisfy prior predicates — row 2 can only be numbered after row 1 is returned, so it's never 'considered' at position 2. Only ROWNUM <= n and ROWNUM = 1 are satisfiable.

drills.q: A colleague imports a MySQL dump; queries using WHERE email <> '' return nothing. Why?
drills.a: Oracle treats the empty string as NULL: '' IS NULL is TRUE, and comparing NULL with <> matches nothing (NULL comparisons are never true). The data didn't vanish — the predicate can never succeed. There is no blank-but-not-null VARCHAR2 in Oracle.

drills.q: A descending salary report shows NULL salaries at the top. Explain and fix — portably.
drills.a: Oracle sorts NULLs as higher than any value: DESC puts them first (ASC last). Fix: ORDER BY salary DESC NULLS LAST. Portable cross-DB: ORDER BY (CASE WHEN salary IS NULL THEN 1 ELSE 0 END) DESC, salary DESC.

drills.q: MERGE throws ORA-30926. What is it and how do you fix it?
drills.a: 'Unable to get a stable set of rows' — multiple staging rows match one target row on the join, so UPDATE is ambiguous. Fix: deduplicate staging (latest-wins via ROW_NUMBER() over the business key) before the MERGE. The error code by symptom is an experience signal.

drills.q: Business demands gapless invoice numbers. Why is a sequence the wrong tool, and what replaces it?
drills.a: Sequences are non-transactional by design — rollback and cache both lose numbers, so gaps are guaranteed; NOCACHE/ORDER kill throughput and still aren't gapless under rollback. Gapless is an accounting requirement: serialized counter table (SELECT ... FOR UPDATE or app-level lock) accepting the serialization cost.

drills.q: Write the org-chart hierarchy as CONNECT BY, then name its modern alternative and the trade.
drills.a: SELECT emp_name, LEVEL FROM employees START WITH manager_id IS NULL CONNECT BY PRIOR emp_id = manager_id; — LEVEL (depth) and SYS_CONNECT_BY_PATH come free; NOCYCLE guards dirty data. Alternative: recursive CTE (11.2+) — portable, composable, depth manual. New code: CTE; read CONNECT BY fluently for maintenance.

drills.q: WHERE date_col BETWEEN SYSDATE-1 AND SYSDATE misses last night's rows. Why?
drills.a: Oracle DATE always carries time-of-day: SYSDATE is 'now with time', so the BETWEEN's start boundary excludes yesterday-evening rows. Fix: TRUNC(SYSDATE)-1 to TRUNC(SYSDATE), or explicit day bounds — the TRUNC habit is institutional for exactly this.

drills.q: Tokyo and London users run the same report; their 'today' rows differ. Which function is the bug and what's the fix?
drills.a: SYSDATE is server-TZ (same for both) — the report must derive day boundaries from CURRENT_DATE (session-TZ), so each user's 'today' is their local today. Real fix: store UTC instants (TIMESTAMP WITH TIME ZONE) and compute local day boundaries at the edge, never in the predicate.

drills.q: NVL vs COALESCE vs DECODE — when does each genuinely win?
drills.a: COALESCE: default (ANSI, lazy per-argument, heterogeneous types). NVL: legacy fluency only — eager evaluation costs with expensive arguments. DECODE: rare legitimate niche — NULL=NULL matching ('did the field change from NULL to NULL' checks), accepting that all branches evaluate.

drills.q: Top 3 per department — write it, and name the RANK/DENSE_RANK/ROW_NUMBER choice.
drills.a: SELECT * FROM (SELECT name, dept, RANK() OVER (PARTITION BY dept ORDER BY salary DESC) rnk FROM employees) WHERE rnk <= 3. RANK: ties share rank, next skips (two firsts -> third gets 3). DENSE_RANK: no skip. ROW_NUMBER: arbitrary unique. 'Top 3' with ties included = RANK; exactly 3 = ROW_NUMBER. 12c+ short-circuits this pattern.

drills.q: Why does SELECT 7*6 FROM employees return many rows, and what is DUAL for?
drills.a: SELECT without aggregation returns one result per row of the FROM table — 7*6 evaluated per employee-row. DUAL is the one-row scratch table for expression evaluation (SELECT 7*6 FROM DUAL; SELECT SYSDATE FROM DUAL): Oracle historically required FROM, DUAL's one-row-ness is the entire point.
